title: The design guide — rule by rule

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about the taste?
steps.changed: Calm, quiet and consistent. One style per job, used everywhere that job appears. The theme decides colour and shape. Text is small, grey and normal-case unless it is the one thing to read; no spaced-out capitals, no redundant labels, one-line headers. Things you open stand out as raised cards; things you read past stay soft. Actions sit on the right: a filled button, switch or chosen option never hangs alone at the bottom-left. When in doubt, remove rather than add.
steps.notice: Sums up your choices; "actions live on the right" is your bottom-left rule.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about principle 1?
steps.changed: 1. Find the job first. Use the recipe below for that job exactly. A new look needs a new job and Destin's approval — never a one-off.
steps.notice: Your "one style per job" direction.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about principle 2?
steps.changed: 2. The theme paints and shapes everything. Colours come from theme tokens; the fixed status hues (green, red, amber, blue) are the only exceptions and go in tints, never in text. Corner roundness comes from the theme's shape setting — never write a fixed pill or pixel radius on a control.
steps.notice: Your "take the theme's roundness" answers; status colour in tints is an existing contrast rule.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about principle 3?
steps.changed: 3. Quiet by default. Small grey labels in normal case. Show what the user needs to act on; drop details nobody asked for. Headers are one line.
steps.notice: No capitals, one-line headers, dropped metadata row.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about principle 4?
steps.changed: 4. Three heading levels, no more. If a screen seems to need a fourth, it needs fewer sections.
steps.notice: Your large / medium / small heading ask.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about principle 5?
steps.changed: 5. Cards stand out; rows stay soft; nothing nests. Things you open are raised cards. Lists of settings are soft boxed rows; pick-one menus are plain rows. Never a box inside a box.
steps.notice: Raised cards, boxed settings rows, plain menus, flat groups.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about principle 6?
steps.changed: 6. Actions live on the right. One filled button per view. A filled button, switch or selection never sits alone at the bottom-left — only when balanced by something on the right of the same line.
steps.notice: Your "left-aligned buttons are broken buttons" note.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about principle 7?
steps.changed: 7. Tight, even spacing from one scale (below).
steps.notice: Your "tighter" Settings pick; the scale itself is my proposal — see Spacing.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about principle 8?
steps.changed: 8. Every theme, every width. Check light, a dark theme, a wallpaper theme and 390px phone width before showing anyone.
steps.notice: Carried over from how every review page was checked.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about full screens?
steps.changed: • The screen names itself centered in the window's top strip, small (14px medium), with its icon. Reference: Pages.  • The way out is a filled small button reading "Esc · Back to chat", top right.  • Big groups on the screen use the *Large* heading.
steps.notice: Your screen-title and way-back picks.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about popups and side panels?
steps.changed: • One shared shell for every popup and side panel (Settings, Session Files, file viewers, Git review, Games, buddy windows): 16px semibold one-line title, the ✕ close button at the right (28px, soft hover square), a tapered line under the header (inset 16px, fading over its first and last 8%). Every popup has the ✕ and closes on Esc.  • When the body scrolls, fade the content at the hidden edge (42px, softened 4% at the sides); no fade when nothing is hidden; never paint a solid strip.  • Narrow popups are up to 420px wide (confirmations, Sound, Create a page); wide popups are larger.
steps.notice: Your title and ✕ picks, the approved line and fade; file viewers, Git review, Games and buddy windows join by your "every popup and side panel" rule. The 420px narrow/wide line is my proposal.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about headings?
steps.changed: • Large — Big groups on a full screen ("Favorites", "Destin's picks"): 18px medium, main text colour.  • Title — A popup or side panel's name: 16px semibold (above).  • Small label — A group inside a screen, popup or list ("Volume", "Privacy"): 12px medium, grey, normal case, no letter-spacing. A small label heading a section of reading text (About's "Disclaimer") also gets a soft underline under its words. Labels over short settings groups stay plain.
steps.notice: Your three levels, no capitals, underlined reading-section labels.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about text and numbers?
steps.changed: • Body 14px; secondary text one grey; the faintest grey only for disabled things.  • Nothing below 11px carries information.  • A count beside a label or tab: the word, then a smaller faint number — "Files 17". In a summary line: bold number, grey word — "17 files". No brackets, no number chips.
steps.notice: Counts are your pick. One grey and the 11px floor are carried over from today — say No if you disagree.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about spacing?
steps.changed: • One scale: 4 · 8 · 12 · 16 · 24 px. 4 between an icon and its label; 8 between things inside a card; 12 inside a card's edge and between cards; 16 between groups; 24 for major breaks.  • In Settings popups: 16px between groups, 6px between rows.
steps.notice: The Settings numbers are your "tighter" pick. The 4 · 8 · 12 · 16 · 24 scale is MY proposal from the spacing audit — the app has no scale today.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about buttons?
steps.changed: • Shape follows the theme's control roundness (built-in themes: Round, 14px).  • Main action: filled. Everything less important beside it (Cancel, Preview, Not now, Dismiss): outlined, never bare text.  • One button: full width.  • Two buttons, side by side (wide popups, chat messages): the filled one on the right, the outlined one directly left of it, both hugging their labels at the right edge.  • Two buttons, stacked (narrow popups and phone width): full width, filled on top.  • Destructive confirm: the red button takes the main action's place — on the right when side by side, on top when stacked.  • Close is always the ✕ button, never a letter or the word.  • Switching views or filters uses the shared tab strip and filter chips, following the same roundness.
steps.notice: Your placement answers. "Both hugging their labels" in wide popups is my reading of your note that equal halves look odd — confirm here.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about settings? The pane shows it.
steps.changed: • Small controls (switches) sit beside the setting's title and hint, on the right. Wide controls (text boxes, sets of choices) go below the title and hint, full width.  • Offering choices: 2–4 short choices → a tab strip; many choices or long names → a dropdown; choices that each need an explanation → a boxed list.  • Groups are flat: a small label, then the rows directly under it, then a normal button. No box inside a box.  • Rows use the shared setting row: title, hint under it in the left column, control at the right.
steps.notice: Your "by control size", flat groups and tighter picks. The choices rule is my proposal for your "it depends".

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about cards? The pane shows it.
steps.changed: • Anything you open, install or pick from a grid is a raised card: panel colour, thin border, a medium shadow, the theme's card corner, 12px between cards. Reference: Your Library.  • Text order: name with its status pill and star on the top line → one row of chips right under the name (trust, who made it, kind, numbers) → the description (two lines at most).  • Conversation cards (Resume, Projects, chat references): name on top with the tag and note buttons at the top right; the date at the bottom right, at the end of the details line.
steps.notice: The pane shows the chip-row card you asked for (U-1). Conversation cards are on the next slide.

steps.headline: Is this the conversation card you meant: buttons top right, date bottom right?
steps.changed: Conversation cards (Resume, Projects, chat references): name on top with the tag and note buttons at the top right; the date at the bottom right, at the end of the details line.
steps.notice: Your U-2 note said "maybe" — this confirms it.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about lists and menus?
steps.changed: • Settings-style lists (each row opens or changes a setting): boxed rows — each row a soft tinted box with a small gap. Reference: the Settings list.  • Pick-one menus and switchers (right-click menu, session list): plain rows — no box, no line; hover highlights; the selected row always looks different from a hovered one.
steps.notice: Your boxed-settings and plain-menu picks; "selected looks different from hovered" fixes a bug the review found.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about status and notices?
steps.changed: • A status label is a small tinted pill in its status colour, normal case ("Installed"). A live status (a session Working / Inactive) carries its coloured dot inside the pill.  • A passive warning, info or danger notice is a tinted box with a matching border. Reference: Backup & Sync → "conversations too big to sync".  • Errors follow docs/error-message-standards.md.
steps.notice: Your tinted-pill and tinted-box picks.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about building a page?
steps.changed: Pages use the page kit's classes (.yc-button, .yc-card, .yc-title, .yc-muted…), which carry these recipes; theme colour and shape reach the page automatically. Follow this guide where a class leaves a choice open, and never restyle a kit class.
steps.notice: The Pages kit will be updated to match before the blind test.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about what is not covered?
steps.changed: These are not final and are exempt from this guide until their own redesign: tool cards, permission prompts (Yes · Always Allow · No stays as today) and the terminal view, which stays exactly as it is.
steps.notice: Tool cards and permission prompts: your call. The terminal: MY call after the confusing question — it simply stays as it is. Say No to revisit it with pictures.

steps.headline: Should the guide say this about the checklist?
steps.changed: ☐ Every element matches a recipe here; nothing invented.  ☐ No hard-coded colour, pill or corner size; theme colours and shape only.  ☐ No spaced-out capitals; headings from the three levels.  ☐ Actions on the right; one filled button; nothing filled alone at the bottom-left.  ☐ Spacing from the scale; no box inside a box.  ☐ Popups have the ✕ and close on Esc.  ☐ Checked in light, a dark theme, a wallpaper theme and at 390px wide.  ☐ Shown to Destin as pictures of the real screen, not described in words.
steps.notice: The last check before anything is shown to you.
